scope: post hoc retained ML draws; proposal only
diagnosis: At fixed positive misfit, variance inflation shrinks with sample size: delta .4 median RMSEA ratios are 1.708, 1.311, 1.166, 1.058 at N=200,500,1000,4000 (CFI: 1.696,1.309,1.146,1.059); mean coverage falls from about .958 to .911/.913. Inflation is largest in long/correlated CFA and somewhat stronger for VM. At delta zero about 99.4-99.9% of intervals clip, and inversion only recovers the truncated point, so ratios there are selected and cannot identify variance bias. The most likely explanation is finite-sample plug-in variance inflation, compatible with a quadratic contribution already entering fitted casewise V1 and then being added again as V2; endpoint data cannot distinguish the components or prove double counting. The smallest future-study comparator is V1 alone when corrected discrepancy is clearly positive, with a prespecified boundary rule and fresh coverage evaluation; do not simply remove V2 near zero. No decision or library change follows.
